I’m considering whether there’s a bore along the beam from the center to the endpoint. FACE3 stretches from x19 to 160 with a radius of 3.175, indicating a tube or bore along the positive half of the member. However, I note the outer beam extends both ways, suggesting a potential through bore only on one end. In the top view, I can see a hole at the right end.

part.name: Crossed-arm central pivot and clamp assembly
part.description: Three-solid assembly consisting of two elongated crossed support arms, a pair of opposed rounded-square hub blocks, and a central cylindrical pivot stack. The arms have flat and rounded longitudinal surfaces, local hub clearances, transverse locating holes near the center, and axial end bores. The opposed hub blocks form a protective clamp or bearing housing around the arm intersection.
part.symmetry_note: The hub and pivot stack are approximately mirror-symmetric about the arm mid-plane y=6.35 mm. Each long arm is approximately two-ended and centered on the hub, but the two arms have different in-plane orientations and local interface details. The complete assembly is therefore not fully rotationally symmetric.

Section.name: Diagonal support arm
features included: Central cylindrical clearance around the pivot
Two transverse locating or fastener holes near the hub
Local shoulders and blended hinge-interface transitions
Section.function intent: Provide the diagonal load-carrying member, connect a remote attachment point to the central hub, and allow the arm to be located or articulated at the hub.
Section.physical behavior: The long section resists axial load and bending. Its rounded longitudinal surfaces reduce edge stress and improve handling, while the broad flat faces carry bending stress. The central clearance and transverse holes locate the arm relative to the pivot hardware. The axial end bore provides a pin, cable, rod, or fastener interface at the positive diagonal end.

Section.location: Extends from the lower-left/rear side of the hub to the upper-right/front side in the front view; represented by STEP SOLID 0.
